claim: Visceral adiposity confers significant risk for developing metabolic disease in obesity.
source: Visceral adiposity confers significant risk for developing metabolic disease in obesity whereas preferential expansion of subcutaneous white adipose tissue (WAT) appears protective.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations in the introduction section.

claim: Preferential expansion of subcutaneous white adipose tissue appears protective in obesity.
source: Visceral adiposity confers significant risk for developing metabolic disease in obesity whereas preferential expansion of subcutaneous white adipose tissue (WAT) appears protective.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations in the introduction.

claim: Visceral WAT is resistant to adopting a protective thermogenic phenotype characterized by the accumulation of Ucp1+ beige/BRITE adipocytes.
source: Unlike subcutaneous WAT, visceral WAT is resistant to adopting a protective thermogenic phenotype characterized by the accumulation of Ucp1+ beige/BRITE adipocytes (termed 'browning').
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations in the introduction.

claim: Zfp423 is a transcriptional suppressor of the adipocyte thermogenic program.
source: In this study, we investigated the physiological consequences of browning murine visceral WAT by selective genetic ablation of Zfp423, a transcriptional suppressor of the adipocyte thermogenic program.
evidence: This is supported by prior work from the authors cited in the introduction.

claim: Zfp423 deletion in fetal visceral adipose precursors (Zfp423loxP/loxP; Wt1-Cre) results in the accumulation of beige-like thermogenic adipocytes within multiple visceral adipose depots.
source: Zfp423 deletion in fetal visceral adipose precursors (Zfp423loxP/loxP; Wt1-Cre), or adult visceral white adipose precursors (PdgfrbrtTA; TRE-Cre; Zfp423loxP/loxP), results in the accumulation of beige-like thermogenic adipocytes within multiple visceral adipose depots.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including gene expression, histology, and oxygen consumption measurements.

claim: Zfp423 deletion in adult visceral white adipose precursors (PdgfrbrtTA; TRE-Cre; Zfp423loxP/loxP) results in the accumulation of beige-like thermogenic adipocytes within multiple visceral adipose depots.
source: Zfp423 deletion in fetal visceral adipose precursors (Zfp423loxP/loxP; Wt1-Cre), or adult visceral white adipose precursors (PdgfrbrtTA; TRE-Cre; Zfp423loxP/loxP), results in the accumulation of beige-like thermogenic adipocytes within multiple visceral adipose depots.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including gene expression, histology, and oxygen consumption measurements.

claim: Thermogenic visceral WAT improves cold tolerance in obese mice.
source: Thermogenic visceral WAT improves cold tolerance and prevents and reverses insulin resistance in obesity.
evidence: This is supported by cold tolerance test data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Thermogenic visceral WAT prevents insulin resistance in obesity.
source: Thermogenic visceral WAT improves cold tolerance and prevents and reverses insulin resistance in obesity.
evidence: This is supported by glucose tolerance tests, insulin tolerance tests, and hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp data presented in Figure 8.

claim: Thermogenic visceral WAT reverses insulin resistance in obesity.
source: Thermogenic visceral WAT improves cold tolerance and prevents and reverses insulin resistance in obesity.
evidence: This is supported by glucose tolerance tests and insulin tolerance tests in the iMural-KO model treated with β3-agonist presented in Figure 10.

claim: White adipocytes serve as the principal site for energy storage in mammals.
source: White adipocytes serve as the principal site for energy storage in mammals.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: White adipocytes are characterized by a large unilocular lipid droplet.
source: These cells are characterized by a large unilocular lipid droplet and have the capacity to store or release energy depending on metabolic demand.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: White adipocytes have the capacity to store or release energy depending on metabolic demand.
source: These cells are characterized by a large unilocular lipid droplet and have the capacity to store or release energy depending on metabolic demand.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: White adipocytes produce and secrete numerous cytokines and hormones that impact several aspects of physiology.
source: White adipocytes also produce and secrete numerous cytokines and hormones that impact several aspects of physiology (Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rosen and Spiegelman, 2014.

claim: Thermogenic adipocytes consist of brown and beige/BRITE adipocytes.
source: These thermogenic adipocytes, consisting of brown and beige/BRITE adipocytes, are characterized by their multilocular lipid droplet appearance, high mitochondrial content, and expression of uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1) (Cohen and Spiegelman, 2015; Harms and Seale, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cohen and Spiegelman, 2015 and Harms and Seale, 2013.

claim: Thermogenic adipocytes are characterized by their multilocular lipid droplet appearance.
source: These thermogenic adipocytes, consisting of brown and beige/BRITE adipocytes, are characterized by their multilocular lipid droplet appearance, high mitochondrial content, and expression of uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1) (Cohen and Spiegelman, 2015; Harms and Seale, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cohen and Spiegelman, 2015 and Harms and Seale, 2013.

claim: Thermogenic adipocytes are characterized by high mitochondrial content.
source: These thermogenic adipocytes, consisting of brown and beige/BRITE adipocytes, are characterized by their multilocular lipid droplet appearance, high mitochondrial content, and expression of uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1) (Cohen and Spiegelman, 2015; Harms and Seale, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cohen and Spiegelman, 2015 and Harms and Seale, 2013.

claim: Thermogenic adipocytes are characterized by expression of uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1).
source: These thermogenic adipocytes, consisting of brown and beige/BRITE adipocytes, are characterized by their multilocular lipid droplet appearance, high mitochondrial content, and expression of uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1) (Cohen and Spiegelman, 2015; Harms and Seale, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cohen and Spiegelman, 2015 and Harms and Seale, 2013.

claim: Activation of brown/beige adipocytes in the setting of obesity has a profound impact on metabolic health.
source: Brown/beige adipocytes have promising therapeutic potential as their activation in the setting of obesity has a profound impact on metabolic health.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations in the introduction.

claim: Adipose tissue distribution is a strong predictor of metabolic outcome in obese individuals.
source: Adipose tissue distribution is a strong predictor of metabolic outcome in obese individuals (Karpe and Pinnick, 2015; Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Karpe and Pinnick, 2015 and Lee et al., 2013.

claim: Visceral adiposity strongly correlates with the development of insulin resistance, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease.
source: Visceral adiposity strongly correlates with the development of insulin resistance, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease (Kissebah et al., 1982; Krotkiewski et al., 1983; Ohlson et al., 1985; Vague, 1956).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kissebah et al., 1982; Krotkiewski et al., 1983; Ohlson et al., 1985; Vague, 1956.

claim: Preferential expansion of subcutaneous depots is associated with sustained insulin sensitivity.
source: Preferential expansion of subcutaneous depots is associated with sustained insulin sensitivity (Manolopoulos et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Manolopoulos et al., 2010.

claim: Transgenic animals overexpressing adiponectin develop extreme subcutaneous obesity but remain metabolically healthy.
source: Transgenic animals overexpressing adiponectin or mitoNEET develop extreme subcutaneous obesity; however, these animals remain metabolically healthy (Kim et al., 2007; Kusminski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2007 and Kusminski et al., 2012.

claim: Transgenic animals overexpressing mitoNEET develop extreme subcutaneous obesity but remain metabolically healthy.
source: Transgenic animals overexpressing adiponectin or mitoNEET develop extreme subcutaneous obesity; however, these animals remain metabolically healthy (Kim et al., 2007; Kusminski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2007 and Kusminski et al., 2012.

claim: The location of visceral adipose tissue itself likely mediates some of its detrimental effects on energy metabolism through direct drainage into the portal circulation.
source: In humans, the location of visceral adipose tissue itself likely mediates some of its detrimental effects on energy metabolism; lipids, metabolites, and cytokines can drain directly into the portal circulation and affect liver function (Rytka et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Rytka et al., 2011.

claim: Factors intrinsic to visceral and subcutaneous adipose depots may determine their effect on nutrient homeostasis.
source: Transplantation studies, cellular studies, and gene expression analyses, suggest that factors intrinsic to these depots may also determine their effect on nutrient homeostasis (Tran et al., 2008; Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tran et al., 2008 and Yamamoto et al., 2010.

claim: Anatomically distinct adipocytes are functionally unique, differing in their ability to undergo lipolysis, lipogenesis, and activate the thermogenic gene program.
source: Anatomically distinct adipocytes are functionally unique, differing in their ability to undergo lipolysis, lipogenesis, and activate the thermogenic gene program (Lee et al., 2013; Macotela et al., 2012; Morgan-Bathke et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2013; Macotela et al., 2012; Morgan-Bathke et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2012.

claim: Anatomically distinct white adipocytes can originate from developmentally distinct precursor cells.
source: Along these lines, lineage analyses reveal that anatomically distinct white adipocytes can originate from developmentally distinct precursor cells, and emerge at different times during development (Billon and Dani, 2012; Chau et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Billon and Dani, 2012 and Chau et al., 2014.

claim: Anatomically distinct white adipocytes emerge at different times during development.
source: Along these lines, lineage analyses reveal that anatomically distinct white adipocytes can originate from developmentally distinct precursor cells, and emerge at different times during development (Billon and Dani, 2012; Chau et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Billon and Dani, 2012 and Chau et al., 2014.

claim: Visceral and subcutaneous adipocytes represent distinct subtypes of fat cells.
source: As such, it is now widely believed that visceral and subcutaneous adipocytes represent distinct subtypes of fat cells.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge and the preceding citations.

claim: Upon high-fat diet feeding, visceral adipose depots of mice expand by both adipocyte hypertrophy and through the formation of new adipocytes.
source: Upon high-fat diet feeding, visceral adipose depots of mice expand by both adipocyte hypertrophy and through the formation of new adipocytes ('adipogenesis') (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2013.

claim: Inguinal subcutaneous WAT expands predominantly through adipocyte hypertrophy upon high-fat diet feeding.
source: Inguinal subcutaneous WAT expands predominantly through adipocyte hypertrophy.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge and the preceding citation.

claim: The differential capacity for adipogenesis between visceral and subcutaneous depots is likely explained by factors present in the local microenvironment.
source: The differential capacity for adipogenesis is likely explained by factors present in the local microenvironment (Jeffery et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jeffery et al., 2016.

claim: β3-adrenergic receptor-agonism and cold exposure drive the rapid accumulation of beige adipocytes in subcutaneous depots.
source: Various stimuli, including β3-adrenergic receptor-agonism and cold exposure, drive the rapid accumulation of beige adipocytes in subcutaneous depots (Vitali et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Vitali et al., 2012 and Wu et al., 2012.

claim: Genetic stimulation of subcutaneous beige adipogenesis renders mice resistant to high-fat diet induced obesity and/or diabetes.
source: Genetic stimulation of subcutaneous beige adipogenesis renders mice resistant to high-fat diet induced obesity and/or diabetes (Seale et al., 2011; Shao et al., 2016), while inhibition of subcutaneous beiging leads to an earlier onset of insulin resistance during obesity (Cohen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Seale et al., 2011 and Shao et al., 2016.

claim: Inhibition of subcutaneous beiging leads to an earlier onset of insulin resistance during obesity.
source: Genetic stimulation of subcutaneous beige adipogenesis renders mice resistant to high-fat diet induced obesity and/or diabetes (Seale et al., 2011; Shao et al., 2016), while inhibition of subcutaneous beiging leads to an earlier onset of insulin resistance during obesity (Cohen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cohen et al., 2014.

claim: Most visceral depots in mice, particularly the gonadal and mesenteric adipose tissues, are relatively resistant to browning in response to physiological stimuli.
source: Most visceral depots in mice, particularly the gonadal and mesenteric adipose tissues, are relatively resistant to browning in response to physiological stimuli.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Most engineered mouse models of white adipose tissue browning exhibit beige cell accumulation preferentially in subcutaneous WAT depots.
source: With few exceptions (Kiefer et al., 2012), most engineered mouse models of white adipose tissue browning exhibit beige cell accumulation preferentially in subcutaneous WAT depots (Seale et al., 2011; Stine et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kiefer et al., 2012; Seale et al., 2011; Stine et al., 2016.

claim: Zfp423 is required for fetal differentiation of subcutaneous white adipocytes.
source: Zfp423 is required for fetal differentiation of subcutaneous white adipocytes (Gupta et al., 2010; Shao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gupta et al., 2010 and Shao et al., 2017.

claim: In adult mice, Zfp423 expression defines a subset of committed mural preadipocytes.
source: In adult mice, Zfp423 expression defines a subset of committed mural preadipocytes (Gupta et al., 2012; Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gupta et al., 2012 and Vishvanath et al., 2016.

claim: Upon high-fat diet feeding, mural cells undergo adipogenesis in visceral depots, contributing to adipocyte hyperplasia.
source: Upon high-fat diet feeding, these mural cells undergo adipogenesis in visceral depots, contributing to adipocyte hyperplasia (Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vishvanath et al., 2016.

claim: Zfp423 is expressed in nearly all mature adipocytes.
source: Zfp423 is also expressed in nearly all mature adipocytes; however, its expression is more abundant in white adipocytes than brown adipocytes (Shao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Shao et al., 2016.

claim: Zfp423 expression is more abundant in white adipocytes than brown adipocytes.
source: Zfp423 is also expressed in nearly all mature adipocytes; however, its expression is more abundant in white adipocytes than brown adipocytes (Shao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Shao et al., 2016.

claim: In the mature adipocyte, Zfp423 acts to maintain the energy-storing status of the white adipocyte through suppression of the thermogenic gene program.
source: In the mature adipocyte, Zfp423 acts to maintain the energy-storing status of the white adipocyte through suppression of the thermogenic gene program (Shao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Shao et al., 2016.

claim: Zfp423 likely exerts its function by serving as a transcriptional co-repressor of the brown/beige lineage determining transcription factor, Ebf2.
source: Zfp423 likely exerts this function by serving as a transcriptional co-repressor of the brown/beige lineage determining transcription factor, Ebf2.
evidence: This is supported by prior work from the authors.

claim: The loss of Zfp423 in mature white adipocytes triggers a robust conversion of white to beige adipocytes in subcutaneous WAT.
source: The loss of Zfp423 in mature white adipocytes triggers a robust conversion of white to beige adipocytes in subcutaneous WAT.
evidence: This is supported by prior work from the authors cited as Shao et al., 2016.

claim: Visceral WAT expresses the highest levels of Zfp423 amongst the various adipose tissues.
source: Amongst the various adipose tissues, visceral WAT expresses the highest levels of Zfp423.
evidence: This is supported by prior work from the authors.

claim: Visceral adipocytes lacking Zfp423 are capable of inducing their thermogenic gene program when animals are stimulated pharmacologically with a β3 adrenergic receptor agonist.
source: Importantly, we observed that visceral adipocytes lacking Zfp423 were also capable of inducing their thermogenic gene program when animals were stimulated pharmacologically with a β3 adrenergic receptor agonist (Shao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Shao et al., 2016.

claim: Vis-KO mice were born in the expected Mendelian ratio and appeared grossly indistinguishable from controls.
source: Vis-KO mice were born in the expected Mendelian ratio and appeared grossly indistinguishable from controls.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiments.

claim: There was no difference in body weight between eight weeks-old Vis-KO mice and littermate controls.
source: We did not observe a difference in body weight between eight weeks-old Vis-KO mice and littermate controls; however, we did observe a noticeable difference in body fat distribution (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Vis-KO mice had smaller gonadal WAT depots compared to control animals.
source: In comparison to control animals, Vis-KO mice had smaller gonadal WAT depots and larger subcutaneous inguinal WAT (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Vis-KO mice had larger subcutaneous inguinal WAT compared to control animals.
source: In comparison to control animals, Vis-KO mice had smaller gonadal WAT depots and larger subcutaneous inguinal WAT (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: mRNA levels of adipocyte-selective genes in visceral adipose depots from the Vis-KO were comparable to levels found in control animals.
source: mRNA levels of adipocyte-selective genes in visceral adipose depots from the Vis-KO were comparable to levels found in control animals (Figure 1E); these data suggest that visceral adipocyte differentiation per se does not depend on Zfp423.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Visceral adipocyte differentiation per se does not depend on Zfp423.
source: mRNA levels of adipocyte-selective genes in visceral adipose depots from the Vis-KO were comparable to levels found in control animals (Figure 1E); these data suggest that visceral adipocyte differentiation per se does not depend on Zfp423.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: In all visceral depots examined, there was a marked increase in the expression of key genes involved in adipocyte thermogenesis, including Ucp1, in Vis-KO mice.
source: However, in all visceral depots examined, there was a marked increase in the expression of key genes involved in adipocyte thermogenesis, including Ucp1 (Figure 1F–G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1F-G.

claim: Visceral depots lacking Zfp423 exhibit increased basal O2 consumption rates.
source: This was accompanied by an increase in basal O2 consumption rates in explanted WAT depots (Figure 1H–J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1H-J.

claim: Some visceral depots (mesenteric and retroperitoneal) lacking Zfp423 exhibit a multilocular appearance typical of thermogenic adipocytes.
source: Furthermore, some visceral depots (mesenteric and retroperitoneal) lacking Zfp423 exhibit a multilocular appearance typical of thermogenic adipocytes (Figure 1L–O, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–L).
evidence: This is supported by histological images shown in Figure 1L-O and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-L.

claim: Inactivation of Zfp423 in fetal visceral white adipocyte precursors leads to the widespread accumulation of beige-like thermogenic adipocytes within visceral adipose depots.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that inactivation of Zfp423 in fetal visceral white adipocyte precursors leads to the widespread accumulation of beige-like thermogenic adipocytes within visceral adipose depots.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Despite the fact that Zfp423 was not inactivated in the subcutaneous inguinal WAT of Vis-KO animals, the thermogenic capacity of this depot was also enhanced.
source: Interestingly, despite the fact that Zfp423 was not inactivated in the subcutaneous inguinal WAT of Vis-KO animals, the thermogenic capacity of this depot was also enhanced (Figure 1F,G,K).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1F, G, and K.

claim: SVF cultures obtained from the inguinal WAT of control and Vis-KO animals differentiated to a similar degree.
source: SVF cultures obtained from the inguinal WAT of control and Vis-KO animals differentiated to a similar degree, and no significant differences in levels of Zfp423 or thermogenic genes were observed (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: No significant differences in levels of Zfp423 or thermogenic genes were observed in inguinal SVF cultures from control and Vis-KO animals.
source: SVF cultures obtained from the inguinal WAT of control and Vis-KO animals differentiated to a similar degree, and no significant differences in levels of Zfp423 or thermogenic genes were observed (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: The increased inguinal WAT beiging in Vis-KO mice in vivo occurs secondary to inactivation of Zfp423 in the Wt1 lineage.
source: This is consistent with lack of Cre activity in this depot, and suggests that the increased inguinal WAT beiging in Vis-KO mice in vivo occurs secondary to inactivation of Zfp423 in the Wt1 lineage.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of Cre activity in inguinal WAT and the observed phenotype.

claim: Cultures of gonadal WAT SVF from control and mutant animals underwent adipogenesis to a similar degree.
source: Cultures of gonadal WAT SVF from control and mutant animals also underwent adipogenesis to a similar degree under the differentiation conditions utilized (dexamethasone, IMBX, insulin, and rosiglitazone). This was evident by comparable lipid accumulation and mRNA levels of adipocyte-selective genes in differentiated cultures (Figure 2A,D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A and D.

claim: Zfp423 mRNA was almost entirely absent from gonadal SVF cultures of Vis-KO mice.
source: Importantly, Zfp423 mRNA was almost entirely absent from these cultures, reflecting the activity of the Wt1-Cre line in this depot.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data from cultured cells.

claim: Cultures of gonadal white adipocytes lacking Zfp423 robustly activate their thermogenic gene program upon stimulation with forskolin.
source: Cultures of gonadal white adipocytes lacking Zfp423 robustly activate their thermogenic gene program upon stimulation with forskolin (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Differentiated gonadal adipocyte cultures from mutant animals exhibit increased basal, uncoupled (oligomycin), and maximal (FCCP) respiration.
source: These changes were accompanied by increased basal, uncoupled (oligomycin), and maximal (FCCP) respiration in differentiated gonadal adipocyte cultures from mutant animals (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F and G.

claim: Zfp423-deficient visceral adipose precursors can differentiate into functional thermogenic adipocytes in a cell-autonomous manner.
source: These data indicate that Zfp423-deficient visceral adipose precursors can differentiate into functional thermogenic adipocytes in a cell-autonomous manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the in vitro differentiation data presented in Figure 2.

claim: The cellular phenotype of Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes is reminiscent of the characterized phenotype of subcutaneous beige adipocyte cultures.
source: The cellular phenotype of Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes is reminiscent of the characterized phenotype of subcutaneous beige adipocyte cultures (Wu et al., 2012); therefore, we examined whether Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocyte cultures are enriched in the expression of beige-selective transcripts.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison to published data from Wu et al., 2012.

claim: Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes expressed lower levels of white adipocyte-selective genes.
source: Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes expressed lower levels of white adipocyte-selective genes; however, we did not observe a clear pattern of gene expression changes that would indicate a conversion of Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes to either subcutaneous beige or classic brown fat cells (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: There was no clear pattern of gene expression changes that would indicate a conversion of Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes to either subcutaneous beige or classic brown fat cells.
source: Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes expressed lower levels of white adipocyte-selective genes; however, we did not observe a clear pattern of gene expression changes that would indicate a conversion of Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes to either subcutaneous beige or classic brown fat cells (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Genetic ablation of Prdm16 in adipose tissue leads to the loss of subcutaneous beige adipocytes, with inguinal WAT acquiring the molecular properties of visceral fat.
source: Prior studies of the beige adipocyte determination factor, Prdm16, revealed that genetic ablation of Prdm16 in adipose tissue leads to the loss of subcutaneous beige adipocytes, with inguinal WAT acquiring the molecular properties of visceral fat.
evidence: This is supported by prior published studies on Prdm16.

claim: CL316,243 treatment led to a much greater increase in mRNA levels of Ucp1 and most other thermogenic genes examined in visceral WAT depots of Vis-KO mice than in control animals.
source: CL316,243 treatment led to a much greater increase in mRNA levels of Ucp1 and most other thermogenic genes examined in visceral WAT depots of Vis-KO mice than in control animals (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Levels of Ucp1 mRNA in the visceral depots lacking Zfp423 nearly reached levels of Ucp1 found in inguinal WAT following CL316,243 treatment.
source: Levels of Ucp1 mRNA in the visceral depots lacking Zfp423 nearly reached levels of Ucp1 found in inguinal WAT following CL316,243 treatment (i.e. subcutaneous beige adipose tissue) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: CL316,243 treatment was accompanied by the widespread appearance of multilocular cells in gonadal WAT with readily detectable Ucp1 protein expression in Vis-KO mice.
source: This was accompanied by the widespread appearance of multilocular cells in gonadal WAT with readily detectable Ucp1 protein expression (Figure 3C–F).
evidence: This is supported by histological images shown in Figure 3C-F.

claim: The global gene expression profile of Zfp423-deficient gWAT is distinct from subcutaneous beige adipose tissue and classic BAT.
source: Principal component analysis and unsupervised hierarchical clustering analysis of RNA-Seq data suggest that the global gene expression profile of Zfp423-deficient gWAT is distinct from subcutaneous beige adipose tissue and classic BAT.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: The Zfp423-deficient visceral WAT more closely resembles gWAT from control animals than subcutaneous beige adipose tissue or classic BAT.
source: Instead, the Zfp423-deficient visceral WAT more closely resembles gWAT from control animals (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Zfp423-deficiency led to the differential expression of 1735 transcripts in gWAT (FDR < 0.05).
source: Zfp423-deficiency led to the differential expression of 1735 transcripts in gWAT (FDR < 0.05) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Of the 1735 differentially expressed transcripts in Zfp423-deficient gWAT, 207 genes (12%) overlap with genes differentially regulated following β3-agonist treatment of iWAT.
source: Of these 1735 transcripts, 207 genes (12%) overlap with genes differentially regulated following β3-agonist treatment of iWAT (Figure 4—source data 3).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Nearly all of the 207 overlapping genes are related to mitochondrial function and biogenesis.
source: Functional classification of these 207 genes by gene ontology analysis indicated that nearly all of these genes are related to mitochondrial function and biogenesis, a hallmark of thermogenic adipocytes (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: Zfp423-deficient adipocytes present in Vis-KO animals are visceral adipocytes expressing at least a portion of the thermogenic gene program characteristic of subcutaneous beige adipocytes.
source: These data suggest that Zfp423-deficient adipocytes present in Vis-KO animals are visceral adipocytes expressing at least a portion of the thermogenic gene program characteristic of subcutaneous beige adipocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the RNA-seq data analysis presented in Figure 4.

claim: Following 1 week of cold exposure, visceral WAT depots of the Vis-KO mice activated their thermogenic gene program to a much greater extent than control animals.
source: Following 1 week of cold exposure, visceral WAT depots of the Vis-KO mice activated their thermogenic gene program (Figure 5A,B) and accumulated Ucp1+ multilocular adipocytes (Figure 5C–J) to a much greater extent than control animals.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5A-J.

claim: Following 1 week of cold exposure, visceral WAT depots of the Vis-KO mice accumulated Ucp1+ multilocular adipocytes to a much greater extent than control animals.
source: Following 1 week of cold exposure, visceral WAT depots of the Vis-KO mice activated their thermogenic gene program (Figure 5A,B) and accumulated Ucp1+ multilocular adipocytes (Figure 5C–J) to a much greater extent than control animals.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5C-J.

claim: There was no significant difference in core body temperature during an acute cold tolerance test of control and Vis-KO animals.
source: We did not observe a significant difference in core body temperature during an acute cold tolerance test of control and Vis-KO animals (Figure 5K); however, after four weeks of cold acclimation, the Vis-KO mice maintain higher core body temperature (Figure 5L).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5K.

claim: After four weeks of cold acclimation, the Vis-KO mice maintain higher core body temperature than control animals.
source: We did not observe a significant difference in core body temperature during an acute cold tolerance test of control and Vis-KO animals (Figure 5K); however, after four weeks of cold acclimation, the Vis-KO mice maintain higher core body temperature (Figure 5L).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5L.

claim: Inactivation of Zfp423 is sufficient to unlock the thermogenic activity of visceral WAT depots under postnatal physiological conditions.
source: Collectively, these data demonstrate that inactivation of Zfp423 is sufficient to unlock the thermogenic activity of visceral WAT depots under postnatal physiological conditions, and that browning of these depots can functionally enhance adaptive thermogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cold exposure data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Browning of visceral depots can functionally enhance adaptive thermogenesis.
source: Collectively, these data demonstrate that inactivation of Zfp423 is sufficient to unlock the thermogenic activity of visceral WAT depots under postnatal physiological conditions, and that browning of these depots can functionally enhance adaptive thermogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cold exposure data presented in Figure 5.

claim: There was no significant difference in body weight between Vis-KO mice and controls over 20 weeks of high-fat diet feeding.
source: Over this period, we did not observe a significant difference in body weight between Vis-KO mice and controls (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: At 8 weeks of HFD feeding, there was no significant difference in adiposity (% body fat), lean mass, or fat distribution between Vis-KO mice and controls.
source: At the time of analysis (8 weeks of HFD feeding), we did not observe a significant difference in adiposity (% body fat), lean mass, or fat distribution (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: The loss of Zfp423 expression remained restricted to visceral depots in obese Vis-KO mice.
source: Gene expression analysis of dissected tissues revealed that the loss of Zfp423 expression remained restricted to visceral depots (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Levels of Ucp1 and other genes related to thermogenesis were significantly increased in visceral depots of obese Vis-KO mice.
source: Levels of Ucp1 and other genes related to thermogenesis were significantly increased in visceral depots of obese Vis-KO mice (Figure 6E,F); however, mRNA levels of adipocyte-selective genes did not appear to be impacted by the loss of Zfp423 (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6E and F.

claim: mRNA levels of adipocyte-selective genes did not appear to be impacted by the loss of Zfp423 in obese Vis-KO mice.
source: Levels of Ucp1 and other genes related to thermogenesis were significantly increased in visceral depots of obese Vis-KO mice (Figure 6E,F); however, mRNA levels of adipocyte-selective genes did not appear to be impacted by the loss of Zfp423 (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Zfp423-deficiency did not impact de novo visceral adipocyte differentiation that occurs during HFD feeding.
source: The later suggests that Zfp423-deficiency did not impact de novo visceral adipocyte differentiation that occurs over this period of HFD feeding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Rates of basal and maximal oxygen consumption were significantly elevated in the visceral depots of obese Vis-KO mice when compared to controls.
source: The increase in thermogenic gene expression appeared functionally significant; rates of basal and maximal oxygen consumption were significantly elevated in the visceral depots of obese Vis-KO mice when compared to controls (Figure 6H–J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6H-J.

claim: There was a slight increase in the expression of thermogenic genes in the inguinal WAT of obese mutant animals.
source: We again observed a slight increase in the expression of thermogenic genes in the inguinal WAT of mutant animals; however, the metabolic activity of the inguinal WAT depot did not significantly differ from inguinal WAT of obese control mice (Figure 6K).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6K.

claim: The metabolic activity of the inguinal WAT depot did not significantly differ from inguinal WAT of obese control mice.
source: We again observed a slight increase in the expression of thermogenic genes in the inguinal WAT of mutant animals; however, the metabolic activity of the inguinal WAT depot did not significantly differ from inguinal WAT of obese control mice (Figure 6K).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6K.

claim: Visceral WAT deletion of Zfp423 enhances energy expenditure.
source: These new data indicate that visceral WAT deletion of Zfp423, and subsequent visceral browning, enhances energy expenditure, albeit not a strong enough degree to drive a robust difference in body weight.
evidence: This is supported by metabolic cage data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Visceral WAT deletion of Zfp423 does not enhance energy expenditure to a strong enough degree to drive a robust difference in body weight.
source: These new data indicate that visceral WAT deletion of Zfp423, and subsequent visceral browning, enhances energy expenditure, albeit not a strong enough degree to drive a robust difference in body weight.
evidence: This is an inference based on the metabolic cage data shown in Figure 7 and body weight data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Obese Vis-KO mice exhibited significantly better glucose tolerance than obese control animals.
source: Obese Vis-KO mice exhibited significantly better glucose tolerance test than obese control animals; excursions in blood glucose and serum insulin following glucose challenge were substantially lower in Vis-KO animals (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: Excursions in blood glucose and serum insulin following glucose challenge were substantially lower in obese Vis-KO animals compared to controls.
source: Obese Vis-KO mice exhibited significantly better glucose tolerance test than obese control animals; excursions in blood glucose and serum insulin following glucose challenge were substantially lower in Vis-KO animals (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: Insulin tolerance tests suggest greater systemic insulin sensitivity in the obese Vis-KO mice.
source: Insulin tolerance tests suggest greater systemic insulin sensitivity in the Vis-KO mice (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The glucose infusion rate needed to maintain euglycemia was increased in obese Vis-KO mice during hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp assays.
source: The glucose infusion rate needed to maintain euglycemia (~138 mg/dl) was increased in Vis-KO mice (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp assays demonstrate an increase in whole-body insulin sensitivity in obese Vis-KO mice.
source: This demonstrates an increase in whole-body insulin sensitivity, consistent with the aforementioned insulin tolerance tests.
evidence: This is an inference based on the clamp data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Endogenous glucose output was suppressed much more efficiently during the basal and clamped states in obese Vis-KO mice.
source: Importantly, endogenous glucose output was suppressed much more efficiently during the basal and clamped states in Vis-KO mice, likely reflecting improved insulin sensitivity at the level of the liver (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The suppression of endogenous glucose output in obese Vis-KO mice likely reflects improved insulin sensitivity at the level of the liver.
source: Importantly, endogenous glucose output was suppressed much more efficiently during the basal and clamped states in Vis-KO mice, likely reflecting improved insulin sensitivity at the level of the liver (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is an inference based on the clamp data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The mRNA levels of key gluconeogenic genes in the Vis-KO livers are significantly lower than corresponding levels in livers from control animals after 8 weeks of HFD feeding.
source: These data are supported by liver gene expression analysis from a separate cohort of animals. The mRNA levels of key gluconeogenic genes in the Vis-KO livers are significantly lower than corresponding levels in livers from control animals after 8 weeks of HFD feeding (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Visceral adipose-selective browning phenotype is associated with lower serum triglyceride levels.
source: Furthermore, visceral adipose-selective browning phenotype is associated with lower serum triglyceride levels (Figure 8G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8G.

claim: The rate of whole-body glucose disposal did not significantly differ between control and obese Vis-KO mice.
source: 14C-2-deoxyglucose tracing revealed that the rate of whole-body glucose disposal did not significantly differ between control and Vis-KO mice (Figure 8H); however, glucose uptake was enhanced in the visceral rWAT depot, correlating with where the largest degree of visceral beiging is observed in this model (Figure 8I).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8H.

claim: Glucose uptake was enhanced in the visceral rWAT depot of obese Vis-KO mice, correlating with where the largest degree of visceral beiging is observed in this model.
source: 14C-2-deoxyglucose tracing revealed that the rate of whole-body glucose disposal did not significantly differ between control and Vis-KO mice (Figure 8H); however, glucose uptake was enhanced in the visceral rWAT depot, correlating with where the largest degree of visceral beiging is observed in this model (Figure 8I).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8I.

claim: Visceral deletion of Zfp423 leads to enhanced insulin sensitivity and reduced hepatic glucose output.
source: All together, these data demonstrate visceral deletion of Zfp423 leads to enhanced insulin sensitivity and reduced hepatic glucose output.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the metabolic phenotyping data presented in Figure 8.

claim: Engineered thermogenic visceral adipose tissue can defend against the development of impaired glucose and lipid homeostasis in obesity.
source: Moreover, these data suggest that engineered thermogenic visceral adipose tissue, much like subcutaneous beige adipose tissue, can defend against the development of impaired glucose and lipid homeostasis in obesity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the metabolic phenotyping data presented in Figure 8.

claim: Adipocytes emerging in expanding visceral WAT depots of diet-induced obese mice arise through de novo adipocyte differentiation from mural progenitors expressing Pdgfrb.
source: We previously demonstrated that adipocytes emerging in expanding visceral, but not subcutaneous, WAT depots of diet-induced obese mice arise through de novo adipocyte differentiation from mural progenitors expressing Pdgfrb (Hepler et al., 2017; Vishvanath et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hepler et al., 2017 and Vishvanath et al., 2016.

claim: Treatment of adult animals with doxycycline leads to Cre dependent inactivation of mural cell Zfp423 in the iMural-KO model.
source: Treatment of adult animals with doxycycline leads to Cre dependent inactivation of mural cell Zfp423 (Figure 9B), and permanent fluorescent-tagging (mGFP) of Pdgfrβ+ cells.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Mature adipocytes present at the time of doxycycline treatment are not targeted in the iMural-KO model.
source: Importantly, mature adipocytes present at the time of doxycycline treatment are not targeted (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Only those adipocytes that descend from mural cells following HFD feeding are Zfp423-deficient and will express mGFP in the iMural-KO model.
source: Only those adipocytes that descend from mural cells following HFD feeding are Zfp423-deficient and will express mGFP.
evidence: This is an inference based on the design of the iMural-KO model.

claim: After 8 weeks of HFD feeding, the body weights of iMural-KO animals were indistinguishable from controls.
source: After 8 weeks of HFD feeding, the body weights of mutant animals were indistinguishable from controls (Figure 9D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 9D.

claim: De novo white adipocyte differentiation occurred in gWAT of both control and iMural-KO animals following HFD feeding.
source: De novo white adipocyte differentiation occurred in gWAT of both control and mutant animals; newly derived adipocytes were indicated by the expression of mGFP (Figure 9E–J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 9E-J.

claim: There was no statistically significant difference in the number of mGFP+ adipocytes between control and iMural-KO mice after 8 weeks of HFD feeding.
source: However, we did not observe a statistically significant difference in the number of mGFP+ adipocytes between control and iMural-KO mice (Figure 9K).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 9K.

claim: Approximately 5–15% of gonadal adipocytes present in the gWAT of obese animals descended from mural cells.
source: Overall, ~5–15% of gonadal adipocytes present in the gWAT of these obese animals descended from mural cells.
evidence: This is supported by quantification of mGFP+ adipocytes shown in Figure 9K.

claim: Adult mural progenitors do not require Zfp423 in vivo for their ability to undergo adipocyte differentiation in response to HFD feeding.
source: Despite the fact that Zfp423 expression identifies mural adipose progenitors, these data suggest that adult mural progenitors do not require Zfp423 in vivo for their ability to undergo adipocyte differentiation in response to HFD feeding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that mGFP+ adipocyte numbers were similar between control and iMural-KO mice.

claim: Zfp423-deficient adipocytes originating from mural progenitors in the obese iMural-KO model were not multilocular.
source: Zfp423-deficient adipocytes originating from mural progenitors in the obese iMural-KO model were readily identified by mGFP expression; however, these cells were not multilocular (Figure 9H,I,J).
evidence: This is supported by histological images shown in Figure 9H, I, and J.

claim: The glucose tolerance of obese iMural-KO mice was similar to that of control animals without β3-agonist treatment.
source: Moreover, the glucose tolerance of obese iMural-KO mice was similar to that of control animals (Figure 9L).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 9L.

claim: The thermogenic activity of Zfp423-deficient adipocytes was dependent on active β-adrenergic signaling.
source: Our previous study revealed that the thermogenic activity of Zfp423-deficient adipocytes was dependent on active β-adrenergic signaling (Shao et al., 2016); it is well appreciated that rodent obesity is associated with augmented β-adrenergic receptor signaling (Collins et al., 1999; Collins and Surwit, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Shao et al., 2016.

claim: Rodent obesity is associated with augmented β-adrenergic receptor signaling.
source: Our previous study revealed that the thermogenic activity of Zfp423-deficient adipocytes was dependent on active β-adrenergic signaling (Shao et al., 2016); it is well appreciated that rodent obesity is associated with augmented β-adrenergic receptor signaling (Collins et al., 1999; Collins and Surwit, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Collins et al., 1999 and Collins and Surwit, 2001.

claim: During the 4 weeks of β3-agonist treatment, both control and iMural-KO animals exhibited a similarly mild decrease in body weight.
source: During the 4 weeks of the β3-agonist treatment, both control and iMural-KO animals exhibited a similarly mild decrease in body weight (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: After four weeks of β3-agonist treatment, the gonadal adipose depot mass of iMural-KO mice was significantly smaller than the gWAT mass of treated control mice.
source: However, after four weeks of β3-agonist treatment, the gonadal adipose depot mass of iMural-KO mice was significantly smaller than the gWAT mass of treated control mice (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: β3-agonist treatment did not induce the formation of any additional gonadal or inguinal adipocytes from the Pdgfrb lineage.
source: Immunohistochemistry for mGFP expression revealed that β3-agonist treatment did not induce the formation of any additional gonadal or inguinal adipocytes from the Pdgfrb lineage (Figure 10D–H, Figure 10—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10D-H and Figure 10—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: There was no difference in the numbers of mGFP-labelled adipocytes between control and knockout animals after β3-agonist treatment.
source: We again did not observe a difference in the numbers of mGFP-labelled adipocytes between control and knockout animals (Figure 10—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Mural-cell derived adipocytes in the β3-agonist treated control animals remained unilocular.
source: Mural-cell derived adipocytes in the β3-agonist treated control animals remained unilocular; however, most mGFP+ adipocytes present in β3-agonist treated knockout mice were now multilocular (Figure 10D–H).
evidence: This is supported by histological images shown in Figure 10D-H.

claim: Most mGFP+ adipocytes present in β3-agonist treated iMural-KO mice were multilocular.
source: Mural-cell derived adipocytes in the β3-agonist treated control animals remained unilocular; however, most mGFP+ adipocytes present in β3-agonist treated knockout mice were now multilocular (Figure 10D–H).
evidence: This is supported by histological images shown in Figure 10D-H.

claim: On average, approximately 6% of gonadal adipocytes appeared multilocular in the β3-agonist treated iMural-KO animals.
source: On average, ~6% of gonadal adipocytes appeared multilocular in the iMural-KO animals; very few, if any, gonadal multilocular adipocytes were present in β3-agonist treated control mice (Figure 10—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Very few, if any, gonadal multilocular adipocytes were present in β3-agonist treated control mice.
source: On average, ~6% of gonadal adipocytes appeared multilocular in the iMural-KO animals; very few, if any, gonadal multilocular adipocytes were present in β3-agonist treated control mice (Figure 10—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Levels of Ucp1 mRNA were strongly elevated in visceral depots of the β3-agonist treated iMural-KO mice.
source: Levels of Ucp1 mRNA were strongly elevated in visceral depots of the β3-agonist treated iMural-KO mice (Figure 10—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The percentage of inguinal adipocytes appearing multilocular appeared low (~3%) and comparable between control and knockout animals after β3-agonist treatment.
source: On the other hand, the percentage of inguinal adipocytes appearing multilocular appeared low (~3%) and comparable between control and knockout animals (Figure 10—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The iWAT from β3-agonist treated knockout animals had relatively higher levels of Ucp1 mRNA in comparison to controls.
source: However, despite the low and comparable levels of mural cell adipogenesis, the iWAT from β3-agonist treated knockout animals had relatively higher levels of Ucp1 mRNA in comparison to controls (Figure 10—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The recruitment of a relatively low number of beige-like adipocytes appeared sufficient to drive an increase in basal respiration of adipose tissues in β3-agonist treated iMural-KO mice.
source: The recruitment of this relatively low number of beige-like adipocytes appeared sufficient to drive an increase in basal respiration of adipose tissues (Figure 10—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The active thermogenic phenotype of the visceral WAT correlated with markedly improved glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity observed in β3-agonist treated iMural-KO mice.
source: This active thermogenic phenotype of the visceral WAT correlated with markedly improved glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity observed in β3-agonist iMural-KO mice (Figure 10I–K).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 10I-K.

claim: Visceral mural preadipocytes in adult mice can be directed to a dormant beige-like phenotype in the expanding visceral WAT depots of diet-induced obese animals.
source: All together, these data indicate that visceral mural preadipocytes in adult mice can be directed to a dormant beige-like phenotype in the expanding visceral WAT depots of diet-induced obese animals.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in Figures 9 and 10.

claim: Upon activation by β3 adrenergic receptor agonism, beige-like adipocytes derived from mural cells appear to drive an improvement in insulin sensitivity in obese animals.
source: Upon activation by β3 adrenergic receptor agonism, these beige-like adipocytes appear to drive an improvement in insulin sensitivity in obese animals.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in Figure 10.

claim: Adult humans have appreciable amounts of thermogenic adipose tissue consisting of brown and beige adipocytes.
source: It is now certain that adult humans have appreciable amounts of thermogenic adipose tissue consisting of brown and beige adipocytes (Cypess et al., 2013; Shinoda et al., 2015; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cypess et al., 2013; Shinoda et al., 2015; van Marken Lichtenbelt et al., 2009; Virtanen et al., 2009.

claim: Upon activation, thermogenic adipose tissue in lean adults can impact glucose and lipid homeostasis.
source: Upon activation, thermogenic adipose tissue in lean adults can impact glucose and lipid homeostasis (Chondronikola et al., 2014, 2016; Cypess et al., 2015); however, it still remains unclear as to whether sufficient amounts of thermogenic adipose tissue are present in obese individuals to exert beneficial therapeutic effects, even when fully activated.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chondronikola et al., 2014, 2016 and Cypess et al., 2015.

claim: It still remains unclear as to whether sufficient amounts of thermogenic adipose tissue are present in obese individuals to exert beneficial therapeutic effects, even when fully activated.
source: Upon activation, thermogenic adipose tissue in lean adults can impact glucose and lipid homeostasis (Chondronikola et al., 2014, 2016; Cypess et al., 2015); however, it still remains unclear as to whether sufficient amounts of thermogenic adipose tissue are present in obese individuals to exert beneficial therapeutic effects, even when fully activated.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Zfp423 is a suppressor of the thermogenic gene program in adipocytes.
source: We recently reported that Zfp423 is a suppressor of the thermogenic gene program in adipocytes.
evidence: This is supported by prior work from the authors.

claim: The thermogenic potential of visceral adipose depots in mice can be unlocked through removal of Zfp423.
source: Using this discovery as a tool, we reveal here that the thermogenic potential of visceral adipose depots in mice can be unlocked through removal of Zfp423.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: White adipose precursors in adult animals can be redirected to a beige-like adipocyte fate and improve insulin sensitivity in obesity.
source: Importantly, these data provide proof of concept that white adipose precursors in adult animals can be redirected to a beige-like adipocyte fate and improve insulin sensitivity in obesity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript, particularly the iMural-KO model.

claim: Elevated expression of Zfp423 in visceral white adipocytes provides one explanation as to how visceral WAT depots resist adopting a thermogenic phenotype.
source: Elevated expression of Zfp423 in visceral white adipocytes provides one explanation as to how visceral WAT depots resist adopting a thermogenic phenotype; however, it remains unclear as to why visceral WAT depots would adopt these anti-thermogenic mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data presented in the manuscript and prior work.

claim: Inactivation of Zfp423 in visceral WAT gives rise to thermogenic adipocytes that share properties of subcutaneous beige adipocytes and classic brown adipocytes.
source: Inactivation of Zfp423 in visceral WAT gives rise to thermogenic adipocytes that share properties of subcutaneous beige adipocytes and classic brown adipocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the gene expression and functional data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Zfp423 deletion in visceral WAT unlocks a functionally significant portion of the thermogenic gene program characteristic of activated beige adipose tissue.
source: In particular, Zfp423 deletion in visceral WAT unlocks a functionally significant portion of the thermogenic gene program characteristic of activated (β3 adrenergic receptor activated) beige adipose tissue.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the RNA-seq data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Zfp423-deficient visceral WAT largely retains a visceral WAT molecular signature, rather than adopting the global molecular program characteristic of subcutaneous WAT.
source: Nevertheless, global gene expression profiling suggests that Zfp423-deficient visceral WAT largely retains a visceral WAT molecular signature, rather than adopting the global molecular program characteristic of subcutaneous WAT.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the RNA-seq data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Most thermogenic adipocytes in visceral WAT are devoid of Ucp1 protein and instead employ futile creatine cycling for thermogenesis.
source: During preparation of this manuscript, Kirichok and colleagues reported the existence of two distinct types of thermogenic beige adipocytes present in visceral depots of mice stimulated with the β3-adrenergic receptor agonist for 10 days (Bertholet et al., 2017). In particular, Bertholet et al. revealed that most thermogenic adipocytes in visceral WAT are devoid of Ucp1 protein and instead employ futile creatine cycling for thermogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bertholet et al., 2017.

claim: Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes express Ucp1 protein.
source: Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes express Ucp1 protein; however, the precise contribution of Ucp1-mediated uncoupling vs. creatine cycling in these cells remains unclear.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: The precise contribution of Ucp1-mediated uncoupling vs. creatine cycling in Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes remains unclear.
source: Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes express Ucp1 protein; however, the precise contribution of Ucp1-mediated uncoupling vs. creatine cycling in these cells remains unclear.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study.

claim: Thermogenic adipocytes, even within the visceral compartment, can drive vast improvements in nutrient homeostasis in obese mice, without impacting body weight.
source: Our data here highlight the ability of thermogenic adipocytes, even within the visceral compartment, to drive vast improvements in nutrient homeostasis in obese mice, without impacting body weight.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the metabolic phenotyping data presented in Figures 6-8.

claim: A relatively low frequency of activated multilocular Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes (5–10% of adipocytes in β3-agonist treated obese iMural-KO mice) can lead to improved insulin sensitivity.
source: Moreover, the mural cell knockout model of Zfp423 even suggests that a relatively low frequency of activated multilocular Zfp423-deficient visceral adipocytes (5–10% of adipocytes in β3-agonist treated obese iMural-KO mice) can lead to improved insulin sensitivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in Figure 10.

claim: It remains an open question as to how brown/beige adipocytes exert beneficial effects on systemic metabolism, independent of their impact on body weight.
source: For the field at large, it remains an open question as to how brown/beige adipocytes exert beneficial effects on systemic metabolism, independent of their impact on body weight.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Previously reported work on Prdm16 and subcutaneous WAT beiging suggest a strong connection between subcutaneous beige cells and liver health.
source: It is notable that in the Vis-KO model, the data largely point to the liver as a major site of improved insulin sensitivity. Previously reported work on Prdm16 and subcutaneous WAT beiging suggest a strong connection between subcutaneous beige cells and liver health (Cohen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cohen et al., 2014.

claim: Zfp423 is a physiological suppressor of the thermogenic gene program in visceral WAT.
source: Together, these data establish Zfp423 as a physiological suppressor of the thermogenic gene program in visceral WAT and provide proof of concept that the thermogenic capacity of visceral WAT can be induced under physiological conditions through removal of this molecular brake on the thermogenic gene program in adipose precursors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The thermogenic capacity of visceral WAT can be induced under physiological conditions through removal of Zfp423 in adipose precursors.
source: Together, these data establish Zfp423 as a physiological suppressor of the thermogenic gene program in visceral WAT and provide proof of concept that the thermogenic capacity of visceral WAT can be induced under physiological conditions through removal of this molecular brake on the thermogenic gene program in adipose precursors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Visceral WAT has the potential to improve nutrient homeostasis in obesity when a thermogenic beige-like phenotype is induced.
source: These data also highlight the potential of visceral WAT, much like subcutaneous WAT, to improve nutrient homeostasis in obesity when a thermogenic beige-like phenotype is induced.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Wt1-Cre mice targets Wt1-expressing cells of the embryonic mesothelium, as well as descending cells, which include adult mesothelial cells and intra-abdominal stromal cells within or surrounding visceral organs.
source: Wt1-Cre mice targets Wt1-expressing cells of the embryonic mesothelium, as well as descending cells, which include, adult mesothelial cells and intra-abdominal stromal cells within or surrounding visceral organs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Wt1-Cre mouse line.

claim: Visceral white adipocytes, but not subcutaneous or classic brown adipocytes, descend from Wt1-expessing progenitors and are targeted by Wt1-Cre.
source: Hastie and colleagues revealed that visceral white adipocytes, but not subcutaneous or classic brown adipocytes, descend from Wt1-expessing progenitors and are targeted by Wt1-Cre (Chau et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chau et al., 2014.

claim: Wt1-Cre targets the majority of gonadal adipocyte precursors and variable numbers of precursors in other visceral depots, including the mesenteric and retroperitoneal depots.
source: Specifically, Wt1-Cre targets the majority of gonadal adipocyte precursors and variable numbers of precursors in other visceral depots, including the mesenteric and retroperitoneal depots.
evidence: This is supported by the citation to Chau et al., 2014 and the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Distinct transcriptional regulatory mechanisms govern fetal vs. adult adipogenesis.
source: These data, along with other studies, highlight the emerging concept that distinct transcriptional regulatory mechanisms govern fetal vs. adult adipogenesis (Jeffery et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jeffery et al., 2015 and Wang et al., 2015.

claim: There are depot-specific requirements of pro-adipogenic transcription factors.
source: Our data here further highlight the complexity in the regulation of adipogenesis in vivo by demonstrating the depot-specific requirements of pro-adipogenic transcription factors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript showing that Zfp423 is required for subcutaneous but not visceral adipogenesis.

claim: Levels of Zfp423 in white adipocytes are reduced following cold exposure and β-adrenergic receptor agonism.
source: Levels of Zfp423 in white adipocytes are reduced following cold exposure and β-adrenergic receptor agonism, and increased in brown adipose depots undergoing a 'whitening' transformation with age or in obesity (Shao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Shao et al., 2016.

claim: Levels of Zfp423 are increased in brown adipose depots undergoing a 'whitening' transformation with age or in obesity.
source: Levels of Zfp423 in white adipocytes are reduced following cold exposure and β-adrenergic receptor agonism, and increased in brown adipose depots undergoing a 'whitening' transformation with age or in obesity (Shao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Shao et al., 2016.

claim: The dynamic expression of Zfp423, along with the loss of function data from genetic mouse models, reveals Zfp423 as a critical physiological suppressor of the adipocyte thermogenic gene program.
source: The dynamic expression of Zfp423, along with the loss of function data from our genetic mouse models, reveals Zfp423 as a critical physiological suppressor of the adipocyte thermogenic gene program.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data presented in the manuscript and prior work.
